pathway.title: CLEVELAND-CLIFFS INC. — Credit Snapshot
pathway.question: Should we own this issuer, in which instrument, and why?

runs.text: Leverage fell sharply but through earnings, not repayment. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 972 replaced 37 for FY2025 as the denominator, with quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 95, 286 and 612 in 2026 (CP-1 Chart data: leverage; Calculations). Because the LTM window still contains weak 2025 quarters, each strong quarter lowers the multiple mechanically, so the 7.93x level is a transition value. If Q3 2026 earnings were annualized, an illustration only, total debt to Adjusted EBITDA would be 3.15x, and the gap between that and 7.93x shows how much of the credit view depends on the recovery persisting. Debt principal fell only from 7,837 at March 31, 2026 to 7,712 at September 30, 2026. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

Interest cover is thin and earnings quality needs a caveat. Cover is 1.84x on cash interest of 529 and 1.61x on net interest expense of 604 over the LTM (CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Adjusted EBITDA includes non-service pension and OPEB credits of 258 over the LTM, equal to 26.5% of Adjusted EBITDA, and these are non-cash while cash pension and OPEB payments were 116 in nine months 2026; excluding them gives leverage of 10.80x (CP-1 Interpretation; Calculations). LTM Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 45.6% before cover on cash interest reached 1.0x, and EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest only 0.70x. The mechanism is that capital expenditure and interest together absorb more than operating earnings, so debt cannot fall from operations alone until earnings rise further. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented figures.

Cash conversion is the weak point. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was negative 332 in nine months 2026 and negative 485 over the LTM, but positive 72 in Q3 2026 (CP-1 Financials and credit metrics). Receivables rose in a rising-price phase (CP-1A Company and operating model, working capital row), so earnings growth was partly absorbed by working capital. Implication: ABL borrowings of 834 remain well above the 452 at December 31, 2025, and liquidity of 3,246 is below the 3,270 at December 31, 2025, despite the earnings recovery. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is back-ended. Cash of 77 and ABL capacity of 3,169 give 3,246, and the only maturity before 2029 is the 834 ABL, due June 2028 or earlier if certain other material debt is near maturity (CP-1 Debt register). The senior notes total 6,878 across nine series, with 1,268 due in 2029 and 6,643 across 2029 to 2034, equal to 86.1% of total debt principal (Calculations). The mechanism is that ABL availability depends on a borrowing base of receivables, inventory and mobile equipment, so liquidity moves with working capital and steel prices, not only with the commitment of 4,750. Category: Documentary Fact.

Structure favours secured lenders, and capacity to add more exists. The ABL has first priority on receivables, inventory and certain mobile equipment and second priority on substantially all other assets, while the notes are unsecured and guaranteed only by domestic subsidiaries (CP-1 Debt register; CP-1A governance register). Management states about 3,000 of secured note capacity (Management Language, carried by CP-1A) that could add debt ranking ahead of the unsecured notes, but no use of it is documented and the indentures are not supplied. Loss-given-default mechanic: priority of claim, not an expected recovery, is what this evidence supports; no recovery outcome is stated. Category: Documentary Fact and Management Language.

Deleveraging sources are management language. Management expects a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter from free cash flow and property sale proceeds, a fourth quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about 715 and 2027 Adjusted EBITDA above 4,000 (CP-1 Latest quarter and events after). With net debt of 7,635 held constant, annualizing the 715 guidance would give net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 2.67x and the 4,000 outlook would give 1.91x (Calculations, illustrations only). The POSCO Memorandum of Understanding is non-binding and subject to definitive terms, the asset sale processes disclose no buyer, price or timing, and the identity of the property sale is not disclosed (CP-1A Transaction summary). The leverage target is worded differently in two releases (CP-0 conflict 2). Category: Management Language; the illustrations are Analyst Interpretation.

Other claims on cash sit outside the debt figure. Finance lease liabilities of 402 at December 31, 2025, unconditional purchase obligations of 13,954 at December 31, 2025, surety instruments of 336 and an employee benefit commitment of 158 at September 30, 2026 are all outside the 7,712 of debt (CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure; CP-1A Transaction summary). Including finance leases of 402, mixed-date, debt to Adjusted EBITDA would be 8.35x. A potential cash call of 500 if Stelco exercises its MinnTac option by January 31, 2027 would reduce liquidity to 2,746 if met from existing liquidity, an assumption (Calculations). Category: Documentary Fact; sensitivities are Analyst Interpretation.

runs.text: Strengths. Liquidity of 3,246, with the 834 ABL as the only maturity before 2029, gives time to execute the recovery, and the 2027 notes were redeemed in October 2025 (CP-1 Chart data; CP-1A Transaction summary). Vertical integration supplies most iron ore, coke, scrap and direct reduced iron internally, which the issuer says makes costs more predictable (Management Language), and the automotive franchise is 30% of 2025 revenue, with about 35-40% of flat-rolled shipments on fixed price contracts that give partial visibility (CP-1A Company and operating model). The loss-making slab contract that was about 10 percent of sales volume expired in December 2025, and CP-1A records a favorable mix effect of about 100 in Q3 2026 Steelmaking revenue. Documented behaviour toward creditors leans supportive: no buybacks since 2024 and a 2025 equity offering of 75 million shares that repaid ABL borrowings (CP-1A governance register). Earnings momentum is documented: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 95, 286 and 612, with price the main driver (CP-1A operating model, price and volume effect row). Category: Documentary Fact except where marked Management Language.

Weaknesses. Leverage of 7.93x total and 7.85x net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA and interest cover of 1.84x leave little margin, and the improvement rests on one strong quarter against a weak 2025 base. Adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash pension credits worth 258 over the LTM, and cash flow after capital expenditure was negative 332 in nine months 2026. The business depends on steel prices and automotive contracts, labor agreements at most steel sites and all iron ore mines expire in 2026 with negotiations ongoing, and six operations were idled or closed in 2025 with further idlings in 2026, creating idle costs that Adjusted EBITDA excludes (CP-1A Company and operating model; Credit translations). The ABL is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes, management cites about 3,000 of secured note capacity, and guarantors are domestic subsidiaries only. Covenant headroom, indentures, ratings, ownership and customer concentration are not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; missing items are Insufficient Information.

runs.text: Stelco acquisition, completed. On November 1, 2024 the issuer completed the Stelco Acquisition under an Arrangement Agreement, as acquirer, paying total purchase consideration of $3,208 million, made up of cash of 2,450, share exchange consideration of 343 (25.9 million treasury shares) and debt consideration of 415 (US$ millions) (10-K page:124, page:157). The stated purpose was to expand the Canadian presence and diversify the customer base toward spot sales, and management says its exposure to the North American spot market "doubled" (10-K page:9, page:10). From a creditor view the mechanism is that the deal added debt and spot-price exposure at a time when Canadian conditions were weak: the Q3 10-Q says Canada imposed tariff-rate quotas on steel imports in the second half of 2025 and that weak demand for value-added sheet products in Canada led to the indefinite idling of finishing operations at Hamilton Works (10-Q Q3 page:29, page:37). Stelco holds an option to buy a 25% interest in the MinnTac iron ore mine from U. S. Steel for $500 million, exercisable until January 31, 2027, carried as a derivative with a fair value of 54 at January 1, 2026 and 16 at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:20). If exercised, the cash call of $500 million would be a liquidity use; whether management intends to exercise is not stated in the sources, and January 31, 2027 is a future date, not an event of the reporting periods. Stelco also carries an employee benefit commitment recorded at $158 million at September 30, 2026 (169 at January 1, 2026) with fixed payments to 2042 plus a variable component (10-Q Q3 page:20).

New debt issues and repayments, completed. In 2025 the issuer issued 850 of 7.500% Senior Notes due 2031 at par under an indenture dated February 6, 2025, and 850 of 7.625% Senior Notes due 2034 at par under an indenture dated September 8, 2025, followed by a further 275 of the 7.625% notes on October 10, 2025 at 102.750% of principal (10-K page:133, page:134). On October 3, 2025 the net proceeds of the 7.625% notes were used to redeem all 685 of the 2027 notes outstanding (73 of 7.000% 2027 notes, 56 of 7.000% 2027 AK Steel notes and 556 of 5.875% 2027 notes), which removed the 2027 maturity wall (10-K page:140). All new notes are unsecured senior obligations guaranteed by the material domestic subsidiaries, are structurally subordinated to non-guarantor debt, and carry "no financial covenants" (10-K page:133, page:134). The issuer sold 75 million common shares in an underwritten offering at $12.69 per share on October 31, 2025 and used the net proceeds to repay ABL borrowings (10-K page:157). No senior notes were issued in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and ABL borrowings rose by 383 over that period to fund general corporate requirements (10-Q Q3 page:45). The liquidity effect is that these actions extended the nearest note maturity to 2029 and used equity to reduce secured ABL borrowings in 2025, then 2026 working capital absorbed part of the benefit. Debt and liquidity figures are in CP-1 and are not repeated here.

Proposed or unfinished transactions. The POSCO Memorandum of Understanding was signed in the third quarter of 2025; POSCO seeks to use the issuer's U.S. footprint, UBS is financial advisor, and the arrangement "remains subject to negotiation of definitive terms" with no assurance that definitive agreements will be signed (10-Q Q3 page:37, page:38). Management expects "substantial proceeds that could be used to reduce our outstanding indebtedness" (Management Language), but the amount, structure and timing are Not disclosed, and the Q1 release says the Middle East situation "has not helped the timeline of a potential deal with POSCO" (Release Q1 page:2). Treat it as a non-binding, unquantified possibility, not a source of repayment. Asset sales: in the third quarter of 2025 the issuer engaged J.P. Morgan and launched sell-side processes for certain non-core operating assets, and received inbound inquiries about idled facilities and inactive sites, intending to use net proceeds to pay down debt (10-K page:9; 10-Q Q1 page:34). Gains on disposal of assets of 23 appear in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:47), and MD&A attributes part of the Miscellaneous, net change to a gain on sale of non-core assets (10-Q Q3 page:43). The Q3 release says "with amplified free cash flow in Q4 and property sale proceeds, we expect a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter" (Release Q3 page:1); no filing identifies the property, buyer, price or closing date. Middletown Works: in the third quarter of 2026 the Department of Energy established a framework to finalize negotiations on a rescoped investment, replacing the previously awarded 500 grant, as a 1,000 total project funded equally by the issuer and the DOE and expected to complete in 2030; the framework is not a signed award (10-Q Q3 page:38, page:39). Subsequent events: the 10-Q Q3 reports none in Note 19, and nothing between October 20, 2026 and 2026-11-05 is supplied. Those are Not supplied, not absent.

Sponsor and ownership transactions. There is no sponsor and no dividend recapitalisation, debt-funded distribution, related-party leakage, priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release in the supplied sources. Share repurchases of 733 in 2024 (37.9 million shares) were followed by none in 2025 and none under the program in the first nine months of 2026, with 1.4 billion of authorization remaining at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:157; 10-Q Q3 page:61). The ABL covenants cover the payment of dividends and the repurchase of capital stock, but no dividend payment line appears in the cash flow statements, and a dividend policy statement is Not supplied (10-K page:139, page:110, page:111).

fields.value: The financial base is usable and the filed numbers tie out across the 10-K, the three 10-Qs and the three releases. Leverage is high but refinancing pressure is back-ended. At September 30, 2026 total debt principal was $7,712 million against cash of $77 million, and LTM Adjusted EBITDA of $972 million gives total debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 7.93x and net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 7.85x. FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA of $37 million makes the FY2025 multiple not meaningful. Liquidity, defined as cash plus ABL borrowing capacity after borrowings and letters of credit, was $3,246 million, and the only covenant the sources describe, a springing fixed charge coverage ratio of 1.0 to 1.0, was not applicable because the ABL liquidity requirements were met. Three restrictions follow every ratio below: Adjusted EBITDA is management's non-GAAP measure and includes non-cash pension and OPEB credits; no indenture or credit agreement is supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable; and lease balances, pension funded status and purchase commitments are available only as of December 31, 2025.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Earnings recovery drives the leverage change. Evidence: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 95, 286 and 612 in 2026 (10-Q Q1 page:41; 10-Q Q2 page:45; 10-Q Q3 page:47) against debt principal that moved only from 7,837 to 7,712. Mechanism: the LTM window still contains the 2025 quarters of weak or negative Adjusted EBITDA (nine months 2025: 58), so each additional strong quarter replaces a weak one and lowers the multiple mechanically. Implication: the 7.93x level is a transition value; if Q3 2026 earnings are annualized (an illustration, not a forecast) the multiple would be 3.15x, so the credit view turns on whether the Q3 run-rate is sustained into the 2027 contract resets management describes. This is an analyst illustration, not a reported or guided figure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Cash conversion is the weak point. Evidence: nine-month 2026 operating cash flow of 129 against capital expenditure of 461, and receivables up by 723 as steel prices rose (10-Q Q3 page:5, page:44). Mechanism: rising prices lift receivables before collections, so earnings growth absorbs working capital in the first half. Implication: debt reduction so far is limited; the sources show ABL borrowings falling by 61 in Q3, and the fourth-quarter reduction management expects is not verifiable.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Quality of Adjusted EBITDA. Evidence: non-service pension and OPEB credits of 258 inside LTM Adjusted EBITDA (223 + 192 - 157) and cash pension and OPEB payments of 116 in nine months 2026 (10-K page:109; 10-Q Q3 page:4, page:5). Mechanism: the credit raises EBITDA without cash. Implication: excluding the credit, LTM Adjusted EBITDA would be 714 and total debt to that figure 10.80x. This sensitivity is analyst-defined and not an issuer measure.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Interest burden. Evidence: the instrument table implies about 519 of annual coupon and ABL interest at current balances (475.7 notes plus 43.5 ABL) against LTM cash interest of 529 and LTM interest expense of 604 (10-Q Q3 page:15, page:9, page:4). Mechanism: expense exceeds the coupon run-rate because of amortization of issuance costs, finance lease interest, fees and other items not itemized. Implication: LTM Adjusted EBITDA covers cash interest 1.84x and interest expense 1.61x, which leaves little room for an earnings reversal.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Maturity profile. Evidence: nothing but the ABL (834, 2028) matures before 2029, and 1,268 matures in 2029 (10-Q Q3 page:16). Mechanism: the secured ABL is a borrowing-base facility whose availability moves with receivables and inventory. Implication: near-term refinancing risk is low on the sources, but 2029 to 2034 carries 6,643 of unsecured notes (1,268 + 750 + 1,175 + 1,425 + 900 + 1,125) before the 2040 notes.

fields.name: Quote

Evidence: note guarantors are described as "material direct and indirect wholly owned domestic subsidiaries" (10-K page:136) and Stelco is a Canadian corporation (10-Q Q3 page:3). Mechanism: if foreign subsidiaries are outside the guarantee group, which the sources imply but do not state, their cash flows and assets support the notes only through the parent. Implication: guarantor-level leverage cannot be computed from the sources; the obligated group summary (10-Q Q3 page:49) is the only guarantor-level data.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cleveland-Cliffs is a publicly listed, vertically integrated flat-rolled steel producer with no sponsor and no controlling owner identified in the supplied sources. Its credit-relevant business facts are a sizeable automotive franchise (30% of 2025 revenue), a mixed pricing model in which about 35-40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed price contracts and the rest follow spot or index prices, internal supply of most iron ore, coke, scrap and direct reduced iron, a unionized workforce with agreements expiring in 2026, and a footprint that management has already trimmed through idlings. The transaction picture is one of completed past actions and unfinished future ones. Completed: the Stelco acquisition on November 1, 2024, the 2025 note issues and the October 2025 redemption of all 2027 notes, and the October 31, 2025 share offering that repaid ABL borrowings. Unfinished: the POSCO Memorandum of Understanding, which is stated to be subject to negotiation of definitive terms; the asset sale processes and the property sale management cites for expected fourth-quarter debt reduction, none of which has a disclosed buyer, price or timing; the Middletown Works investment framework with the Department of Energy; and the MinnTac purchase option. Documented issuer behaviour is mixed to supportive for creditors: share repurchases stopped after 2024, equity was raised in 2025 to repay the ABL, and no priming, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the supplied sources. Legal capacity is a separate question: management states approximately $3 billion of secured note capacity, which could place new secured debt ahead of the unsecured notes if used, and the indentures that govern it are not supplied. Management's own forward statements (fourth quarter outlook, 2027 outlook, leverage target) are attributed and not adopted.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Stelco acquisition, completed. On November 1, 2024 the issuer completed the Stelco Acquisition under an Arrangement Agreement, as acquirer, paying total purchase consideration of $3,208 million, made up of cash of 2,450, share exchange consideration of 343 (25.9 million treasury shares) and debt consideration of 415 (US$ millions) (10-K page:124, page:157). The stated purpose was to expand the Canadian presence and diversify the customer base toward spot sales, and management says its exposure to the North American spot market "doubled" (10-K page:9, page:10). From a creditor view the mechanism is that the deal added debt and spot-price exposure at a time when Canadian conditions were weak: the Q3 10-Q says Canada imposed tariff-rate quotas on steel imports in the second half of 2025 and that weak demand for value-added sheet products in Canada led to the indefinite idling of finishing operations at Hamilton Works (10-Q Q3 page:29, page:37). Stelco holds an option to buy a 25% interest in the MinnTac iron ore mine from U. S. Steel for $500 million, exercisable until January 31, 2027, carried as a derivative with a fair value of 54 at January 1, 2026 and 16 at September 30, 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:20). If exercised, the cash call of $500 million would be a liquidity use; whether management intends to exercise is not stated in the sources, and January 31, 2027 is a future date, not an event of the reporting periods. Stelco also carries an employee benefit commitment recorded at $158 million at September 30, 2026 (169 at January 1, 2026) with fixed payments to 2042 plus a variable component (10-Q Q3 page:20).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: New debt issues and repayments, completed. In 2025 the issuer issued 850 of 7.500% Senior Notes due 2031 at par under an indenture dated February 6, 2025, and 850 of 7.625% Senior Notes due 2034 at par under an indenture dated September 8, 2025, followed by a further 275 of the 7.625% notes on October 10, 2025 at 102.750% of principal (10-K page:133, page:134). On October 3, 2025 the net proceeds of the 7.625% notes were used to redeem all 685 of the 2027 notes outstanding (73 of 7.000% 2027 notes, 56 of 7.000% 2027 AK Steel notes and 556 of 5.875% 2027 notes), which removed the 2027 maturity wall (10-K page:140). All new notes are unsecured senior obligations guaranteed by the material domestic subsidiaries, are structurally subordinated to non-guarantor debt, and carry "no financial covenants" (10-K page:133, page:134). The issuer sold 75 million common shares in an underwritten offering at $12.69 per share on October 31, 2025 and used the net proceeds to repay ABL borrowings (10-K page:157). No senior notes were issued in the nine months ended September 30, 2026 and ABL borrowings rose by 383 over that period to fund general corporate requirements (10-Q Q3 page:45). The liquidity effect is that these actions extended the nearest note maturity to 2029 and used equity to reduce secured ABL borrowings in 2025, then 2026 working capital absorbed part of the benefit. Debt and liquidity figures are in CP-1 and are not repeated here.

fields.value: Proposed or unfinished transactions. The POSCO Memorandum of Understanding was signed in the third quarter of 2025; POSCO seeks to use the issuer's U.S. footprint, UBS is financial advisor, and the arrangement "remains subject to negotiation of definitive terms" with no assurance that definitive agreements will be signed (10-Q Q3 page:37, page:38). Management expects "substantial proceeds that could be used to reduce our outstanding indebtedness" (Management Language), but the amount, structure and timing are Not disclosed, and the Q1 release says the Middle East situation "has not helped the timeline of a potential deal with POSCO" (Release Q1 page:2). Treat it as a non-binding, unquantified possibility, not a source of repayment. Asset sales: in the third quarter of 2025 the issuer engaged J.P. Morgan and launched sell-side processes for certain non-core operating assets, and received inbound inquiries about idled facilities and inactive sites, intending to use net proceeds to pay down debt (10-K page:9; 10-Q Q1 page:34). Gains on disposal of assets of 23 appear in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:47), and MD&A attributes part of the Miscellaneous, net change to a gain on sale of non-core assets (10-Q Q3 page:43). The Q3 release says "with amplified free cash flow in Q4 and property sale proceeds, we expect a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter" (Release Q3 page:1); no filing identifies the property, buyer, price or closing date. Middletown Works: in the third quarter of 2026 the Department of Energy established a framework to finalize negotiations on a rescoped investment, replacing the previously awarded 500 grant, as a 1,000 total project funded equally by the issuer and the DOE and expected to complete in 2030; the framework is not a signed award (10-Q Q3 page:38, page:39). Subsequent events: the 10-Q Q3 reports none in Note 19, and nothing between October 20, 2026 and 2026-11-05 is supplied. Those are Not supplied, not absent.

There is no sponsor and no dividend recapitalisation, debt-funded distribution, related-party leakage, priming, uptiering, drop-down, non-pro-rata exchange or collateral release in the supplied sources. Share repurchases of 733 in 2024 (37.9 million shares) were followed by none in 2025 and none under the program in the first nine months of 2026, with 1.4 billion of authorization remaining at December 31, 2025 (10-K page:157; 10-Q Q3 page:61). The ABL covenants cover the payment of dividends and the repurchase of capital stock, but no dividend payment line appears in the cash flow statements, and a dividend policy statement is Not supplied (10-K page:139, page:110, page:111).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Revenue durability. Evidence: direct automotive was 30% of 2025 revenue and about 35-40% of flat-rolled shipments are on fixed price contracts, the rest spot or index-linked (10-K page:12, page:13). Mechanic: the fixed-price book gives some visibility and resets as contracts renew, while the spot and index book moves with HRC, which averaged $851 per net ton in 2025 and $1,195 in Q3 2026 (10-K page:15; 10-Q Q3 page:28). Implication: earnings and refinancing capacity are tied to the steel price cycle and to the renewal of a few automotive contracts; customer concentration data is Not disclosed, so the size of that exposure cannot be stated. Counter-evidence: no logged conflict changes the revenue picture, but the two leverage-target wordings (CP-0 conflict 2) limit how far management's deleveraging statements can be relied on.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Margin and cash-flow risk. Evidence: Q3 2026 price effect of about 500 on Steelmaking revenue and an accounts receivable build of 723 in nine months 2026 (10-Q Q3 page:40, page:5). Mechanic: higher prices lift revenue before cash is collected, so the first half of a price recovery absorbs working capital. Implication: debt reduction lags earnings, and the management-expected fourth-quarter reduction depends on free cash flow and property sale proceeds that the filings do not quantify.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Concentration and operating risk. Evidence: labor agreements at most major steel sites and all iron ore mines expire in 2026 and negotiations with the USW are ongoing (10-K page:58; 10-Q Q3 page:34); six operations were idled or closed in 2025 and further idlings occurred in 2026 (10-K page:8; 10-Q Q3 page:37). Mechanic: a work stoppage or a cost step-up hits an integrated system where internal supply is a stated advantage, and idle sites carry costs excluded from Adjusted EBITDA. Implication: monitor labor outcomes and idle-cost cash payments (accrued idle liabilities 40 at September 30, 2026).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: - Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor; equity raise and buyback halt documented. Mechanic: management and public shareholders, not a financial sponsor, control creditor-relevant choices. Implication: behaviour so far leans supportive of creditors, but legal capacity for secured debt is wide and the governing documents are not supplied.

The POSCO agreement terms, the identity and size of the property sale, whether the MinnTac option will be exercised, ownership and customer concentration, ratings, and any event after October 20, 2026. Conflicts that counter a clean reading: sell-side language dropped between the Q1 and Q2 10-Qs; "permanently close" versus "indefinitely idle" for Steelton, Conshohocken and Riverdale.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: The fundamental credit view is of a leveraged, cyclical steel producer in the early stage of an earnings recovery, with adequate liquidity and a back-ended maturity profile but thin interest cover and no verified source of near-term debt repayment. Leverage at September 30, 2026 was 7.93x total debt and 7.85x net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 972, down from 25.20x and 25.05x at March 31, 2026, and the improvement came from quarterly Adjusted EBITDA rising from 95 to 286 to 612 across 2026 while debt principal moved only from 7,837 to 7,712. Liquidity of 3,246 is the sum of cash of 77 and ABL capacity of 3,169, set by a borrowing base that moves with receivables and inventory. The ABL, at 834, is the only maturity before 2029 and is secured; the nine unsecured note series follow, with 1,268 due in 2029. Interest cover of 1.84x on cash interest and 1.61x on net interest expense is thin, and Adjusted EBITDA includes non-service pension and OPEB credits worth 258 over the LTM, which are non-cash. The business risk is tied to steel prices, automotive contract resets, labor agreements expiring in 2026 and a footprint that has been trimmed through idlings. Three potential transactions (POSCO, property and non-core asset sales, and the MinnTac option) are unquantified or unresolved and are treated as unverified rather than as support. The view is Analyst Interpretation with Medium confidence. It is not an instrument view and states no recovery outcome.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cleveland-Cliffs is a leveraged cyclical steelmaker whose creditworthiness now depends on holding the 2026 earnings recovery long enough to turn a thin interest cover and 7.93x leverage into real debt reduction, while liquidity of 3,246 and a 2029-weighted maturity profile give it time to do so.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Leverage fell sharply but through earnings, not repayment. LTM Adjusted EBITDA of 972 replaced 37 for FY2025 as the denominator, with quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 95, 286 and 612 in 2026 (CP-1 Chart data: leverage; Calculations). Because the LTM window still contains weak 2025 quarters, each strong quarter lowers the multiple mechanically, so the 7.93x level is a transition value. If Q3 2026 earnings were annualized, an illustration only, total debt to Adjusted EBITDA would be 3.15x, and the gap between that and 7.93x shows how much of the credit view depends on the recovery persisting. Debt principal fell only from 7,837 at March 31, 2026 to 7,712 at September 30, 2026. Category: Documentary Fact for the figures, Analyst Interpretation for the reading.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Interest cover is thin and earnings quality needs a caveat. Cover is 1.84x on cash interest of 529 and 1.61x on net interest expense of 604 over the LTM (CP-1 Chart data: interest cover). Adjusted EBITDA includes non-service pension and OPEB credits of 258 over the LTM, equal to 26.5% of Adjusted EBITDA, and these are non-cash while cash pension and OPEB payments were 116 in nine months 2026; excluding them gives leverage of 10.80x (CP-1 Interpretation; Calculations). LTM Adjusted EBITDA could fall by about 45.6% before cover on cash interest reached 1.0x, and EBITDA less capital expenditure covers cash interest only 0.70x. The mechanism is that capital expenditure and interest together absorb more than operating earnings, so debt cannot fall from operations alone until earnings rise further. Category: Analyst Interpretation on documented figures.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Cash conversion is the weak point. Operating cash flow less capital expenditure was negative 332 in nine months 2026 and negative 485 over the LTM, but positive 72 in Q3 2026 (CP-1 Financials and credit metrics). Receivables rose in a rising-price phase (CP-1A Company and operating model, working capital row), so earnings growth was partly absorbed by working capital. Implication: ABL borrowings of 834 remain well above the 452 at December 31, 2025, and liquidity of 3,246 is below the 3,270 at December 31, 2025, despite the earnings recovery. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Liquidity is adequate and refinancing is back-ended. Cash of 77 and ABL capacity of 3,169 give 3,246, and the only maturity before 2029 is the 834 ABL, due June 2028 or earlier if certain other material debt is near maturity (CP-1 Debt register). The senior notes total 6,878 across nine series, with 1,268 due in 2029 and 6,643 across 2029 to 2034, equal to 86.1% of total debt principal (Calculations). The mechanism is that ABL availability depends on a borrowing base of receivables, inventory and mobile equipment, so liquidity moves with working capital and steel prices, not only with the commitment of 4,750. Category: Documentary Fact.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Structure favours secured lenders, and capacity to add more exists. The ABL has first priority on receivables, inventory and certain mobile equipment and second priority on substantially all other assets, while the notes are unsecured and guaranteed only by domestic subsidiaries (CP-1 Debt register; CP-1A governance register). Management states about 3,000 of secured note capacity (Management Language, carried by CP-1A) that could add debt ranking ahead of the unsecured notes, but no use of it is documented and the indentures are not supplied. Loss-given-default mechanic: priority of claim, not an expected recovery, is what this evidence supports; no recovery outcome is stated. Category: Documentary Fact and Management Language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Deleveraging sources are management language. Management expects a major debt reduction in the fourth quarter from free cash flow and property sale proceeds, a fourth quarter Adjusted EBITDA of about 715 and 2027 Adjusted EBITDA above 4,000 (CP-1 Latest quarter and events after). With net debt of 7,635 held constant, annualizing the 715 guidance would give net debt to Adjusted EBITDA of 2.67x and the 4,000 outlook would give 1.91x (Calculations, illustrations only). The POSCO Memorandum of Understanding is non-binding and subject to definitive terms, the asset sale processes disclose no buyer, price or timing, and the identity of the property sale is not disclosed (CP-1A Transaction summary). The leverage target is worded differently in two releases (CP-0 conflict 2). Category: Management Language; the illustrations are Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Other claims on cash sit outside the debt figure. Finance lease liabilities of 402 at December 31, 2025, unconditional purchase obligations of 13,954 at December 31, 2025, surety instruments of 336 and an employee benefit commitment of 158 at September 30, 2026 are all outside the 7,712 of debt (CP-1 Claims outside the debt figure; CP-1A Transaction summary). Including finance leases of 402, mixed-date, debt to Adjusted EBITDA would be 8.35x. A potential cash call of 500 if Stelco exercises its MinnTac option by January 31, 2027 would reduce liquidity to 2,746 if met from existing liquidity, an assumption (Calculations). Category: Documentary Fact; sensitivities are Analyst Interpretation.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Strengths. Liquidity of 3,246, with the 834 ABL as the only maturity before 2029, gives time to execute the recovery, and the 2027 notes were redeemed in October 2025 (CP-1 Chart data; CP-1A Transaction summary). Vertical integration supplies most iron ore, coke, scrap and direct reduced iron internally, which the issuer says makes costs more predictable (Management Language), and the automotive franchise is 30% of 2025 revenue, with about 35-40% of flat-rolled shipments on fixed price contracts that give partial visibility (CP-1A Company and operating model). The loss-making slab contract that was about 10 percent of sales volume expired in December 2025, and CP-1A records a favorable mix effect of about 100 in Q3 2026 Steelmaking revenue. Documented behaviour toward creditors leans supportive: no buybacks since 2024 and a 2025 equity offering of 75 million shares that repaid ABL borrowings (CP-1A governance register). Earnings momentum is documented: quarterly Adjusted EBITDA of 95, 286 and 612, with price the main driver (CP-1A operating model, price and volume effect row). Category: Documentary Fact except where marked Management Language.

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Weaknesses. Leverage of 7.93x total and 7.85x net debt to LTM Adjusted EBITDA and interest cover of 1.84x leave little margin, and the improvement rests on one strong quarter against a weak 2025 base. Adjusted EBITDA includes non-cash pension credits worth 258 over the LTM, and cash flow after capital expenditure was negative 332 in nine months 2026. The business depends on steel prices and automotive contracts, labor agreements at most steel sites and all iron ore mines expire in 2026 with negotiations ongoing, and six operations were idled or closed in 2025 with further idlings in 2026, creating idle costs that Adjusted EBITDA excludes (CP-1A Company and operating model; Credit translations). The ABL is secured and ranks ahead of the unsecured notes, management cites about 3,000 of secured note capacity, and guarantors are domestic subsidiaries only. Covenant headroom, indentures, ratings, ownership and customer concentration are not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact and Analyst Interpretation; missing items are Insufficient Information.

fields.value: The following located facts are supplied here because the earlier handoffs cannot be edited. In the Q3 10-Q the issuer states that "Finished steel import levels remained significantly below historical levels during the third quarter of 2026, which helped support domestic steel pricing" (S4 page:28). The same page says domestic HRC averaged $1,195 per net ton, "representing a 42% increase compared to the third quarter of 2025". The next page says the President signed a proclamation "to implement 50% tariffs on steel imports originating from all major steel producing countries" during 2025, that an April 2026 proclamation "maintained 50% tariff coverage on steel products", and that "Year-to-date total steel imports through August 2026 declined 15% as compared to the same period in 2025" (S4 page:29). The Q3 release quotes management that "Imports remain well below historical levels" (S7 page:2). The goodwill discussion lists "significant recent shifts in trade policies, including the imposition of tariffs" among conditions that could affect impairment assessments (S4 page:54).

fields.name: Quote
fields.value: Evidence to risk to implication: the HRC price is the index that most affects revenue and profitability (S4 page:28), the price rise is described as supported by low imports and tariffs, so a change in tariff coverage, an increase in import levels or retaliation would lower price and hence LTM Adjusted EBITDA, on which the 7.93x leverage and 1.84x cash interest cover depend (CP-1). The CP-2 sensitivity that a 45.6% fall in LTM Adjusted EBITDA would take cash interest cover to 1.0x gives the scale. The first observable trigger would be import volumes or HRC price moving against the 2026 level in the next filing. This supplement does not change the credit view; it names a driver the view should carry as a Critical or Material risk trigger.
